basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 34.' and it opens 'Vers. 34. Major pars venit Benjamin. Benjamin diximus Paulum apostolum significare, cui'. The printing states no chapter here and the lemma is too short to match, so the chapter is the one the preceding block established.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 34. Major pars venit Benjamin. Benjamin diximus Paulum apostolum significare, cui major pars obvenit, quia plus caeteris in praedicatione laboravit, et ab Jerusalem usque in Illyricum replevit Evangelium Christi.
